channel.title: Ahmet Keles — Writing
channel.description: Notes on backend and distributed systems from things I have built.

item.title: Logic Diagram Tool: from a Boolean equation to the gate diagram and truth table
item.description: A browser tool for digital-logic lab reports. Type a Boolean equation with up to four inputs (A·B, A+B, A', A⊕B, or the words AND/OR/NOT/XOR/NAND/NOR/XNOR) and it draws the ANSI gate diagram with orthogonal wires and junction dots, folds NOT-over-AND/OR/XOR into single NAND/NOR/XNOR gates, builds the full truth table with every intermediate column, and exports SVG or PNG. One HTML file, no dependencies, no network requests.

item.title: A transactional outbox that survives two replicas
item.description: Publishing Kafka events from inside a database transaction is wrong in both directions. The outbox pattern fixes that, but the first outbox I wrote broke as soon as two replicas polled the same table, and the second held locks for 1000 seconds. Here is what it took to make it safe: SKIP LOCKED claims, a bounded lock hold, and a cross-replica ordering guard.

item.title: Idempotent Kafka consumers: the claim goes inside the transaction
item.description: At-least-once delivery means every consumer will eventually see a duplicate. A processed-events ledger handles that, but where you put the ledger write decides whether a retry can lose the event forever. Plus how to classify failures so retries and dead letters do the right thing, and why the ledger's retention bounds the guarantee.

item.title: Drawing wrap-around Karnaugh map loops on a canvas
item.description: A Karnaugh map group can wrap from the top row to the bottom or the left column to the right. Drawing that on a canvas without special-casing every shape came down to one observation about Gray code and open edges. How K-Map Looper turns a set of cells into loop pieces, and why it refuses to solve the map for you.
